sources.name: Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) API
sources.description: Public breach metadata API. Used to cross-check whether a company name appears as a tracked general breach. Requires an API key for full querying; this project only uses the free, unauthenticated 'breach list' style public data where available and never submits user-supplied personal data to it.
sources.license_notes: Subject to HIBP API Terms of Use. This project does not redistribute HIBP's data verbatim; it only checks for name matches against our manually curated ID/age-verification breach list.

methodology_notes: This project only includes breaches with substantive public reporting from at least one credible news, security-research, or company-disclosure source.

Companies with no confirmed public breach are still listed (marked with an empty known_breaches array) to provide comprehensive coverage of the ID/age-verification industry, consistent with the project's goal of tracking the sector as a whole.

Government identity authorities (e.g., France Titres, RENAPER, Aadhaar/UIDAI, Bangladesh NID) are included alongside private vendors where a breach directly involved identity-document or KYC-equivalent data, even though they are not commercial identity-verification companies.
Severity ratings are an editorial judgment based on the number of records affected, sensitivity of data types, and duration/scope of exposure. They are not an official industry standard.

The automation pipeline (GitHub Actions) proposes new candidate entries by keyword-matching company names and breach-related terms in RSS/news feeds; it does not auto-publish claims without a human-reviewable pull request, to avoid propagating unverified rumors as fact.
